thread:
samir: FYI customer 'acme-corp' on Dedicated reported indexing errors after yesterday's model pin change. Error in indexer logs: "vector dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 1024". They see ~20% rejects on backfill.

ingrid: ugh. did they swap models at the application level or did we roll a new model variant on the endpoint?

samir: They switched to a smaller embed model to save cost. App change happened ~03:12 UTC. Indexer started backfill at 03:35. Mixed vectors landed.

kai: quick Q - are rejects coming from the embed service (wrong dim emitted) or from the vector DB (schema enforcement)? any snippets of the reject?

samir: From indexer logs: `indexer-4 | WARN indexer: drop vector id=upsert-12345 reason=dim_mismatch expected=1536 actual=1024`. Downstream DB returns 400 on insert.

josh: Could be batching + config drift: if backfill batches contain some docs produced by new model (1024) and some old (1536) we might be writing into an index whose schema already migrated to 1536.

ingrid: Also check auth/billing — if some embed requests fell back to a smaller free model due to key throttling or quota, that would explain mixed dims. samir can you check telemetry for returned model names and rate-limited responses?

samir: pulling telemetry now. I see ~14% of embedding calls to `embed-prod` responded with model `embed-lite-1024` around 03:10–03:20. There are a few 429s from `billing-proxy` at 03:08.

kai: ok that matches. Two problems: (1) deployment/rollout allowed app to target smaller model; (2) billing throttle caused fallback to lite model for some requests. Both created mixed-dim payloads for the backfill.

josh: Repro plan: 1) replay a small batch where we force some requests to embed-lite-1024 and others to embed-1536, then run indexer against a staging index with schema=1536 to confirm rejects. 2) run a dim-check pre-ingest step in indexer to reject/transform before DB insert.

samir: quick repro script I ran locally (feel free to copy):
```bash
# produce two embeddings, one 1024 and one 1536 (mocked)
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input": "short doc A", "model":"embed-lite-1024"}' > /tmp/e1.json
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input": "short doc B", "model":"embed-pro-1536"}' > /tmp/e2.json
# then feed both to indexer stub
python tools/indexer_stub.py --input /tmp/e1.json /tmp/e2.json --index staging_test
```

ingrid: thanks. For immediate mitigation we should: (a) pause the backfill job, (b) run a detection query on the vector DB to surface all vectors with length != 1536, (c) block writes from legacy models until we finish remediation.

kai: SQL to find bad rows (postgres + pgvector):
```sql
SELECT id, octet_length(vector) / 4 AS dim_estimate FROM vectors WHERE (octet_length(vector) / 4) != 1536 LIMIT 50;
```
Note: `octet_length/4` approximates float4 array length depending on storage, adjust for our DB.

josh: Another quick script to gate ingestion at the indexer level: check `len(vector)` and if len != EXPECTED_DIM then either transform (pad/trim) or enqueue to a remediation stream. I vote for enqueue -> remediation to avoid silent quality loss. :+1:

samir: customer impact: ACME has ~120k documents in backfill, estimated 25k affected. They're paused and asking for ETA.

ingrid: Proposed remediation steps and owners: 
- Pause backfill and confirm paused (samir)
- Run DB detection query and export sample bad ids (kai)
- Determine if impacted vectors came from the same time window / API key / region (samir)
- Decide remediation: re-run embed generation for affected ids with embed-pro-1536 OR reindex from source (josh + acme SE)
- Add temporary indexer dim-check gate and metric (ingrid)
- Fix billing-proxy fallback behavior to not auto-switch models on 429 without explicit config (infra).

josh: timeline: pause + detection in 1h, sample + confirm origin in 2h, remediation plan + cost estimate in 4h. We can offer ACME a bulk re-embed run on Dedicated infra as a one-off.

samir: I've paused the job and uploaded detect sample CSV to the support ticket. Also opened an infra ticket to look into billing-proxy fallback: INFRA-4521.

kai: follow-up action: add a short-lived alert on `indexer.dim_mismatch_rate` > 0.5% to prevent silent regressions.

ingrid: for postmortem items: document rollout checklist to ensure model & index schema compatibility before backfills, add a pre-backfill dim validation step, and update runbooks to include checking billing fallbacks.

samir: I'll reply to customer with plan and estimated window. Thanks all. :pray:
